scope: Align Android Broker signing keys with the repository's hardware-backed Android Key Attestation verifier and permit exact-key P-256 verification in the existing Cloud A2A trust boundary.

research.finding: AOSP Key Attestation schema describes asymmetric key algorithms as RSA, EC, or ML-DSA. The repository's pinned verifier returns a P-256 public point, so the previous Android Ed25519 Broker key could not be established by that verifier.

implemented: Android Broker signing now uses a non-exportable AndroidKeyStore P-256 key with attestation challenge, TEE/StrongBox requirement, and point-digest key ID.
Java ECDSA DER signatures are converted to the 64-byte P1363 encoding used by Cloud WebCrypto; the server request remains domain-separated and owner/device/delegation scoped.
Cloud A2A proof and wallet-handoff verification retain legacy Ed25519 verification and add uncompressed P-256 point verification.

Operator trust inventory accepts exact 32-byte Ed25519 keys or 65-byte uncompressed P-256 points, still bound to authority, owner, device and key ID. It remains operator-controlled; no self-enrollment was added.

notVerified: Android P-256 KeyStore generation, attestation chain, DER-to-P1363 Java code and instrumentation were not compiled or run because Android SDK/JDK are unavailable in this host.
No server challenge/enrollment/revocation API or dynamic Cloud D1 trust-key resolver exists yet; operator trust configuration is still required and currently has no production device keys.
